issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the template Main.java shows example instantiation of Seal, Pig, and Goat using two-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the UML and intended design define Animal with only a 'name' attribute (so subclasses should take a single String name). The solution repository implements single-argument constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat. This inconsistency in the template example can confuse students about the required constructor signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the example code in the template Main.java consistent with the UML and solution by using single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if two attributes are intended, update the UML, Animal class, and all subclass constructors to include and initialize the additional attribute so the template example matches the specification.

issues.description: The commented example code in the template Main uses two-argument constructors for Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the problem description/UML and the solution implementation expect a single-argument constructor that initializes the animal's name (e.g., Seal(String name)). This mismatch in constructor signatures for the same conceptual entities (Seal, Pig, Goat) can confuse students about how to construct these objects and which attributes classes should have.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent across artifacts. Either update the template Main commented code to use single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML/problem and solution, or explicitly document and implement the additional attribute across the problem statement and solution. Prefer updating the template Main to the single-argument form so all artifacts consistently use constructors that take only the animal name.
